description:
Cross-environment overview of the Altinn information portal (Umbraco). Every panel shows AT22, AT23, TT02 and PROD side by side — there is deliberately no environment variable, so a fault can be seen moving up the promotion path without switching views. Environment colours are fixed and identical in every panel.

Application Insights panels are one cross-resource query over the four `dis-core-<env>-products-ai` components (`cloud_RoleName = infoportal`), with the environment derived from `_ResourceId`. Availability comes from the blackbox-exporter probes in `admin-prod-obs-amw`, which only cover PROD (`info.altinn.no`) and AT22 (`info.at22.altinn.cloud`) — AT23 and TT02 have no probe target.

Datasource UIDs are pinned rather than templated: a `${datasource}` variable saves the value `default`, the default datasource here is Azure Monitor rather than Prometheus, and Grafana then silently binds the probe panels to a Prometheus that holds no probe data.

For a PROD-only deep dive — endpoint tables, 404 attribution by caller, dependency detail — see *Infoportal — Service Health (Prod)*.

links.title: Infoportal — Service Health (Prod)
links.tooltip: PROD-only deep dive: endpoints, 404 attribution, dependencies

panels.title: Availability — blackbox /health probes (PROD and AT22 only)
/health probe — now
panels.description:
Deep health check: HTTP 200 **and** a JSON body of `status: Healthy`. For PROD this is the exact series the `Availability Prod` alert evaluates.

Only these two hosts are probed — **AT23 and TT02 have no blackbox target**, so their availability cannot be shown here. Their liveness has to be read off the traffic and error panels below instead.

panels.title: /health availability — selected range
panels.description:
Fraction of the selected range where the deep /health probe passed. Prober pods are collapsed with `max by (instance)` **before** averaging over time, so a short-lived replica cannot mask an outage.

AT22 is a test environment and is routinely torn down or redeployed — red here is normal and is not comparable to red on PROD.

panels.title: TLS certificate expires in
panels.description: Days until the earliest certificate in each host's chain expires.

panels.title: /health probe status over time
panels.description: Up/Down bands for the deep health probe. Outages read as contiguous red blocks; a gap (no band) means the probe itself stopped reporting, which is a different failure from a failing probe.

panels.title: /health probe duration
panels.description: Wall-clock time of the deep health probe. The deep check runs the full application health pipeline, so it is expected to be slower than a shallow HTTP probe; a rising trend is an early warning that the app is degrading before the probe outright fails.

panels.title: All environments at a glance (selected range)
panels.description: One row per environment, ordered AT22 → AT23 → TT02 → PROD (the promotion path). `Err5xx` is the only column that means *broken*: `NotFound` is tracked separately because 404s are the dominant traffic class on this service and would otherwise swamp the error signal, and `P95ms` excludes both 404s and the `/umbraco/serverEventHub` long-poll stream. `Exceptions` counts `traces` at `severityLevel >= 3` — the App Insights `exceptions` table is empty for this service. An environment missing entirely from this table served no requests at all in the selected range.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
let reqs = requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize
    Requests = count(),
    Err5xx   = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500),
    NotFound = countif(toint(resultCode) == 404),
    P95ms    = round(percentile(iff(toint(resultCode) != 404 and name !has "serverEventHub", duration, real(null)), 95), 1)
  by Env;
let errs = traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and severityLevel >= 3
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Exceptions = count() by Env;
reqs
| join kind=leftouter errs on Env
| extend Exceptions = coalesce(Exceptions, 0)
| extend
    Err5xxPct   = round(100.0 * Err5xx / Requests, 3),
    NotFoundPct = round(100.0 * NotFound / Requests, 1)
| extend EnvOrder = case(Env == "AT22", 1, Env == "AT23", 2, Env == "TT02", 3, Env == "PROD", 4, 9)
| project EnvOrder, Env, Requests, Err5xx, Err5xxPct, Exceptions, NotFound, NotFoundPct, P95ms
| order by EnvOrder asc
| project-away EnvOrder

panels.title: Traffic, errors and latency by environment
Requests per interval
panels.description: Log scale: PROD runs two to three orders of magnitude above the test environments, and a linear axis would flatten AT22/AT23/TT02 onto the zero line. A line dropping out entirely means that environment stopped serving traffic.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Requests = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.title: Server error rate (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests returning 5xx, which is comparable across environments in a way that raw counts are not. 404s are deliberately left in the denominator here; because they dominate, this reads low — use the scorecard's `Err5xx` count to judge absolute volume.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize ErrorRatePct = round(100.0 * countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500) / count(), 3)
    by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.title: P95 latency (404s and long-poll excluded)
panels.description: Server-side P95. Two exclusions matter: 404s never reach application code and would drag the percentile down, and `/umbraco/serverEventHub` is a SignalR stream whose requests last minutes by design — leaving it in puts P95 in the millions of milliseconds. Log scale keeps a single slow environment from flattening the rest.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and toint(resultCode) != 404 and name !has "serverEventHub"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize P95ms = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1) by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.title: Not found (404) — share of traffic
panels.description: Tracked apart from errors on purpose. On PROD this sits near 98%: a blanket redirect funnels dead Altinn 2 REST API paths at this host, and CMS content lookups miss frequently. It is a content-quality and legacy-integration signal, not an outage signal — but a sudden change in the shape of this line is worth chasing.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize NotFoundPct = round(100.0 * countif(toint(resultCode) == 404) / count(), 1)
    by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.title: Exceptions (severity ≥ 3)
panels.description: `traces` at `severityLevel >= 3`, the same grouping the `Exceptions Prod` alert fires on. This service writes exceptions into `traces` with OpenTelemetry `customDimensions['exception.type' / 'exception.message']`; the App Insights `exceptions` table is empty.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and severityLevel >= 3
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Errors = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.title: Top exceptions — all environments
panels.description: Grouped exactly as the `Exceptions Prod` alert groups them (Type / Details), with the environment carried alongside so a fault can be seen moving up the promotion path. `Details` is the OpenTelemetry `exception.message` where present, otherwise the raw trace message, truncated to 200 characters.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and severityLevel >= 3
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| extend ExType = tostring(customDimensions["exception.type"])
| extend ExMsg  = tostring(customDimensions["exception.message"])
| extend Details = substring(iff(isnotempty(ExMsg), ExMsg, message), 0, 200)
| summarize Count = count(), LastSeen = max(timestamp) by Env, Type = ExType, Details
| order by Count desc
| take 40

panels.title: Endpoints with 5xx or high latency
panels.description: Only endpoints that actually misbehaved: at least one 5xx, or P95 above one second. Org numbers and GUIDs are normalised to `{orgnr}` / `{guid}` so un-routed paths do not explode into thousands of one-off rows. 404s and the `/umbraco/serverEventHub` long-poll stream are excluded — neither is a fault.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and toint(resultCode) != 404 and name !has "serverEventHub"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| extend Endpoint = replace_regex(
    replace_regex(name, @"/\d{6,}", "/{orgnr}"),
    @"/[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}",
    "/{guid}")
| summarize
    Count  = count(),
    Err5xx = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500),
    P95ms  = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1)
  by Env, Endpoint
| extend Err5xxPct = round(100.0 * Err5xx / Count, 1)
| where Err5xx > 0 or P95ms > 1000
| project Env, Endpoint, Count, Err5xx, Err5xxPct, P95ms
| order by Err5xx desc, P95ms desc
| take 30

panels.title: Outbound dependencies
panels.description: Every outbound call the portal makes, per environment. `InProc` rows are in-process Umbraco handlers rather than network calls — the `HTTP` rows (mail relay, Microsoft Graph, the site search backend) are the ones that can fail on their own and take the portal with them.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-at22", "AT22",
    r has "dis-core-at23", "AT23",
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize
    Calls  = count(),
    Failed = countif(success == false),
    P95ms  = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1)
  by Env, Target = target, Type = type
| extend FailPct = round(100.0 * Failed / Calls, 1)
| project Env, Target, Type, Calls, Failed, FailPct, P95ms
| order by Failed desc, Calls desc
| take 30
